content: AmBisome (liposomal amphotericin B) is a medication used for the treatment of serious fungal infections. It is specifically indicated for the following conditions: 1. Empiric Therapy for Presumed Fungal Infections in Febrile, Neutropenic Patients: The recommended dosage is 3 mg/kg administered intravenously once daily. 2. Treatment of Infections Caused by Aspergillus, Candida, or Cryptococcus Species: This is particularly for cases refractory to amphotericin B deoxycholate or when renal impairment or unacceptable toxicity precludes the use of amphotericin B deoxycholate. The dosage ranges from 3 to 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily. 3. Cryptococcal Meningitis in HIV-Infected Patients: The recommended dosage is 6 mg/kg intravenously once daily. 4. Visceral Leishmaniasis: Note that the relapse rate is high in immunocompromised patients after initial clearance of parasites with liposomal amphotericin B. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends considering a switch to liposomal amphotericin B if a patient is clinically unresponsive to echinocandin treatment or has persistent fungemia for more than five days. The suggested dosage in such cases is 5 mg/kg intravenously once daily. Adverse Effects AmBisome is associated with a range of adverse effects, including but not limited to: Electrolyte Imbalances: Hypokalemia (31-51%), hypomagnesemia (15-50%), and hypocalcemia (5-18%). Systemic Reactions: Chills (29-48%), fever, nausea (16-40%), vomiting (11-32%), diarrhea (11-30%), and rash (5-25%). Hematologic Effects: Anemia (27-48%), leukopenia (15-17%), and thrombocytopenia (6-13%). Renal and Hepatic Effects: Nephrotoxicity (14-47%), increased alkaline phosphatase (7-22%), increased ALT (15%), and increased AST (13%). Cardiovascular and Respiratory Effects: Hypertension (8-20%), hypotension (7-14%), tachycardia (9-19%), dyspnea (18-23%), and pleural effusion (13%). Neurological and Psychological Effects: Insomnia (17-22%), headache (9-20%), confusion (9-13%), and anxiety (7-14%). Other Effects: Infusion reactions (4-21%), peripheral edema (15%), back pain (12%), chest pain (8-12%), and pruritus (11%). Precautions Pregnancy: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Amphotericin B deoxycholate has been used successfully in pregnant women for systemic fungal infections, but the number of reported cases is small. Breastfeeding: It is unknown whether this drug is excreted in human milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, considering the importance of the drug to the mother. Drug Interactions: AmBisome may interact with other medications, potentially altering their effects or increasing the risk of side effects. Patients should maintain a list of all medications and share it with their healthcare provider. Infusion Reactions: These may occur during administration. Symptoms include fever, shaking, chills, flushing, loss of appetite, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, headache, shortness of breath, or rapid breathing. Premedication with acetaminophen, diphenhydramine, or corticosteroids may be prescribed to mitigate these effects. Administration Guidelines AmBisome should be administered intravenously, typically over a period of at least two hours using a controlled infusion device. If well-tolerated, the infusion time may be reduced to one hour. The drug may be infused through an in-line filter with a pore diameter greater than 1 micron. If using an existing IV line, flush the line with D5W (5% dextrose in water) prior to infusion. The medication should be refrigerated at 36-46°F (2-8°C) and should not be frozen. Storage and Handling Inspect the product visually for particles or discoloration before use. Do not use if either is present. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Overdose In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. For U.S. residents, contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring Patients receiving AmBisome should undergo regular laboratory tests to monitor kidney and liver function, electrolyte levels (potassium, magnesium), and complete blood counts. Close clinical observation is recommended during the initial dosing period. Important Notes AmBisome is significantly less toxic than amphotericin B deoxycholate, but adverse events may still occur. This medication is not suitable for noninvasive fungal infections (e.g., oral thrush, vaginal candidiasis) in patients with normal neutrophil counts. Acute pulmonary toxicity has been reported with simultaneous leukocyte transfusions. Therapy should be administered by medically trained personnel, and patients should be under close clinical observation during treatment. This information is not exhaustive and does not replace professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
